Armor isn't about avoiding hits. Hits happen, that's the always-hit rule in action. Armor is what you wear and what you have been through: boiled leather, rings of steel, a breastplate that has already turned one blade. It is a choice about weight, slots, donning time, and what it says about you. What keeps you standing is the steel you wear or the drills you have run, whichever is stronger. Damage Reduction comes from your armor and from your talents.

Shields are different. A shield is not a passive number on your sheet, it is an active defense, something you put in the way of a blow. It gives you a reaction that downgrades an incoming hit. Wear your armor. Use your shield. Choose wisely.

#pagebreak()

== How Damage Reduction Works

When you take physical damage, subtract your Damage Reduction (DR) from the damage value. The remainder is what you actually lose from your HP. A hit always lands for at least 1 damage, no matter how much DR you have. Simple.

Your DR comes from one source at a time: your armor, a talent, or a spell. Armor's DR is set by its weight class: light 1, medium 2, heavy 3. Heavier armor is heavier in every sense, and in the kit builder it costs more points. If more than one source gives you DR, use the highest. Armor, talents, and wards do not add together.

*Shield DR is the exception.* DR from a shield source is *shield DR*. A shield item grants no number on its own; shield DR comes from a card, and Wall Shield and Ward of Faith are the only two printed sources. It adds to your DR from other sources, after the ceiling below. No combination of shield sources ever adds more than +3, so a second shield grant is worth nothing on top of the first.

*There is a ceiling.* Your total DR from armor, talents, and wards cannot exceed 3 at Novice, 4 at Adept, or 6 at Master. A hit must always be able to land for something, and the three tiers of a damage band have to stay distinct at every level. If DR could climb past that ceiling the roll would stop carrying information, and light, medium, and heavy armor would stop being three different choices. The highest source governs up to the ceiling, and no further. Shield DR is added after it.

*Temporary grants add.* DR granted by an ability for a stated duration adds to your DR while it lasts. A temporary grant is not a source you carry: it adds on top of whatever you already have, and it ends when the duration does. Guarding Stance, Warding Touch, Shield of Faith, Bulwark, and Ironhide all work this way.

*Ranks set the size of a grant.* A DR grant requires Discipline ranks at least equal to the DR it grants: DR 2 costs 2 ranks, DR 3 costs 3. The armor table's light 1, medium 2, heavy 3 column is the same scale.

*Example:* Kael wears light armour, so his armour grants DR 1. He is also under Stone Skin, which grants +2 DR. The two are sources and do not add: his DR is the higher of the two, 2. A goblin's scimitar hits him for Weak damage (4). 4 - 2 = 2, so Kael takes 2 damage. When the same goblin lands a Standard hit (6), Kael takes 4 instead of 6.

What you wear is worth its points in DR: light armor grants 1, medium 2, heavy 3. Beyond that, the only other decisions are slots and how long it takes to get into.

== Shields

A shield is an active defense. You're not just wearing it, you're using it. When an attack comes in, you can throw the shield in its path.

The number before each shield is a Discipline requirement: you need that many ranks in the Shields Discipline to wield it, with no exception. The full rules live in @sec-chapter-disciplines

*Buckler:* 1 Shields Discipline. Small, strapped to the forearm. Leaves your hand free for a second weapon or a wand.

*Shield:* 1 Shields Discipline. The standard. Wood and iron, carried in the off hand.

*Tower Shield:* 2 Shields Discipline, half cover. A portable wall. You move at -5 ft speed while carrying it. You can plant it as a maneuver to grant full cover to one ally directly behind you.

=== Shield Block (Reaction)

When you are hit by an attack, you may use your reaction to interpose your shield. Reduce the damage tier by one step: *Strong → Standard, Standard → Weak, Weak → 1 damage.* You must be wielding a shield and be aware of the attack. Reactions in general are covered in @sec-chapter-combat

Shield Block cannot reduce damage below 1. It can be used against melee attacks, ranged attacks, and spell attacks, anything you can see coming.

#quote[*DA Guidance:* Let the player declare Shield Block after hearing the damage tier result, not before. This makes shields feel active and tactical rather than just a passive DR bonus.]

#pagebreak()

== Worked Example: Choosing Your Armor

Roric is building a dwarf Protector at Level 1. He has Brawn +2, Fortitude +1, 13 HP, and 1 Armor Discipline rank. He wants to be the party's wall, but the wall has to fit inside a pack. He has watched the ward ladder work for the party's casters: Bark Skin for +1 DR, Stone Skin for +2, each one self only and sustained by a Maneuver every round. Here's how he weighs his own options:

*Leather:* Light, DR 1, 2 slots, 1 minute to don.

*Chain Mail:* Heavy, DR 3, 4 slots, 10 minutes to don.

With leather his DR is 1. The party's wards are self only, so none of them can cover him, and even if a caster could lay one on him a ward is a source, not an addition: leather plus Stone Skin would be 2, still under the steel, and it would cost a Maneuver every round to hold. With chain mail his DR is 3, the best a ward can reach, and the steel costs no Maneuver to keep. That is the real trade. Chain mail costs two more slots and takes ten minutes to don instead of one, and it never asks a caster to spend a turn on it. Roric takes the chain mail. He would rather carry the weight than stand behind a ward that has to be paid for every round.

Armor is a decision about what the character can carry, what they give up, and how fast they can arm. The DR is what those choices buy, and for the hero already wearing armor a ward is no substitute: the ladder is the unarmored caster's path to the same numbers.

#pagebreak()

== Worked Example: Shield Block in Combat

Roric is holding a choke point against two goblins and their orc warchief. He's wearing the chain mail he chose above, so his armor grants DR 3 all on its own. He's also carrying a shield, and the board in his hand is about to earn its keep. The goblins aren't getting through easily.

Remember how this works. The DA never rolls for monsters (@sec-chapter-combat) The DA describes the attack and names the Challenge, and Roric's player makes the Defense Roll. Strong defense means the blow lands Weak, Standard means it lands Standard, Weak means it lands Strong. Roric has Parry rank 1 and a shield in hand, so he defends with 3d6 + Brawn + Parry rank - Challenge.

*Goblin 1 attacks:* "The goblin comes in low, scimitar slashing at Roric's shins. Challenge 1." Roric rolls 3d6 + Brawn +2 + Parry +1 - 1 = 3d6 + 2. He rolls 3, 4, 4 = 11 + 2 = 13. *Standard.* The scimitar's Standard damage is 6. 6 - 3 = 3 damage. The blade dings off his armor with a sad _ping._

*Goblin 2 attacks:* "The second goblin circles wide, scimitar raised for an overhead cut. Challenge 1." Roric rolls 3d6 + 2. He rolls 1, 2, 3 = 6 + 2 = 8. *Weak.* The blow lands solid: Strong damage, 8. 8 - 3 = 5 damage. Roric doesn't flinch. He's at 5 HP now, and he's only been standing here one round.

*Orc warchief attacks:* "The warchief says nothing. He doesn't need to. His greataxe comes around in a two-handed arc. Challenge 3." This is the one that matters. Roric rolls 3d6 + Brawn +2 + Parry +1 - 3 = 3d6. He rolls 4, 4, 3 = 11. *Standard.* The axe lands for Standard damage: 6.

*Roric's player:* "Shield Block."

He spends his reaction. The damage tier drops one step, Standard to Weak, and the incoming damage is now 4. 4 - 3 = 1 damage. The greataxe slams into Roric's shield, ringing off the boss like a temple bell. The haft cracks at the binding, but the blade never reaches him.

That is 3 + 5 + 1 = 9 damage across the round, and Roric stands at 4 HP of his 13. Without the shield he would have taken 6 - 3 = 3 from that swing, and that is the difference between holding the choke point and going down in it. Shield Block is what the board in his hand is for, because the DR came from his armor alone.

#pagebreak()

== Donning & Doffing

Light armor (Padded, Leather, Studded Leather): 1 minute. Medium armor (Chain Shirt, Breastplate): 5 minutes. Heavy armor (Half Plate, Chain Mail, Plate): 10 minutes. Shield: 1 action.

You won't always have time to suit up. If the party is ambushed while camping, the Protector fights in whatever they were sleeping in. Plan accordingly: sleeping in chain mail is exactly as unpleasant as it sounds.

#callout(type: "note", title: "Armor Isn't the Point", body: [
Your DR is a small, fixed number from your armor, or from a ward when you have no armor to wear. It will not save you from a bad position, and it will not save you from five goblins. Five goblins all attacking the same target will eventually wear down even the toughest Protector through sheer volume of hits.

Use cover. Use positioning. Use the fact that you're harder to kill than everyone else to _control where the fight happens._ The Protector's real armor isn't steel, it's standing in the right place at the right time.
])
